answer: At the market inlet, each agent must lock 100 copper tokens for 30 days to open one bidding slot; splitting into more identities creates no free slots. The scheduler caps each slot at one active job, so an attacker seeking a delta of 1,000 simultaneous bids must immobilize 100,000 tokens. Honest agents recover their bonds after the lock expires, but a sybil swarm pays the opportunity cost of tying up capital for every extra slot.
